title: Align canonical MAP authority hierarchy across operator surfaces
description: Operator-authorized correction after TASK-302 restored the fixed Command Center roster: define one canonical authority hierarchy (bigboss/operator -> one designated coordinator per run -> accountable task owners and conflict-separated independent reviewers -> bounded Pi/Librarian/visible-helper/local support), keep Codex and Claude eligible core agents, distinguish finalized checksum-bound session continuity from governance-role transfer, align governing docs/startup prompts/Command Center presentation, and add contradiction tests without creating a new orchestration subsystem or weakening existing approval/security gates.
acceptance_criteria: project-brief.md contains the single canonical hierarchy: bigboss/operator, one designated coordinator per run, parallel accountable owner and independent reviewer roles, then bounded support; Codex and Claude remain eligible core agents rather than fixed rank holders.

AGENTS rules and every fixed-roster startup prompt reference the canonical hierarchy without claiming that terminal presence, provider, model, SQLite, LangGraph, hcom, or Command Center storage confers authority.

Context rotation states that only a finalized checksum-bound ledger entry transfers explicit continuity and any designated coordinator continuation; prepare or ACK alone does not transfer operator, policy, task-owner, or review authority.
The Command Center Lab presentation makes fixed roster visibility distinct from authority assignment and does not add an orchestration subsystem.
Focused contradiction tests fail on sole-orchestrator claims, fixed provider-to-rank claims, support-role authority escalation, owner/reviewer collapse, or prepare/ACK-as-authority-transfer wording.
Delivery evidence records operator approval source, affected surfaces, focused test results, rollback, residual approval/security boundaries, and operator-friction closeout.
